details: Eval is Python-only in ADK; the Go server exposes ListEvalSets/ListEvalResults routes but they return HTTP 501 via controllers.Unimplemented. No dataset format, runner, or harness ships in adk-go.

Agno ships first-party AccuracyEval / PerformanceEval / ReliabilityEval / AgentAsJudge classes in libs/agno/agno/eval/, with results persisted to the agno_evals table via db.create_eval_run. Not as dataset-centric as pydantic-evals (no separate Dataset/Case file format), but the harness is built in and usable for regression.

No Dataset, no Evaluator, no EvalRun ship in AutoAgents; the report flags 'Not provided — BYO'. A `parallel.rs` evaluator exists in autoagents-llm but it is for internal parallelism, not regression eval.
Report marks this red: no golden-dataset format, no regression harness ships with the Python SDK. You build it yourself around query().
No golden-dataset format and no regression harness; only a SessionStore conformance suite exists (adapter test, not agent regression). Users build eval harnesses themselves over query().

`crewai test [-n N]` runs the crew N times and CrewEvaluator scores task outputs via an LLM, printing a table. However there is no dataset format: you re-run with whatever inputs are in the script (or via kickoff_for_each), so regression suite semantics are partial.
Eino ships no Dataset, no Evaluator, no EvalRun types. Users roll their own with Go's testing package plus recorded model.BaseChatModel mocks.

Genkit Go has first-class Evaluator and Example types (go/ai/evaluator.go) plus built-in deep-equal/regex/jsonata evaluators, with datasets managed via the Genkit CLI. Falls short of 4 because the LLM-as-judge variants live in the JS side and the harness flow depends on the genkit-tools CLI rather than a pure-Go runner.
langgraph OSS ships no dataset or regression suite primitive. The recommended path is LangSmith (paid) for hosted datasets and evaluators, or BYO pytest harness around graph.invoke().

Built-in evaluation primitives under llama-index-core/llama_index/core/evaluation/: RetrieverEvaluator, RelevancyEvaluator, FaithfulnessEvaluator, CorrectnessEvaluator, AnswerRelevancyEvaluator, GuidelineEvaluator, SemanticSimilarityEvaluator, BatchEvalRunner, plus RagDatasetGenerator/LabelledRagDataset. Strong, but heavily RAG-tilted so agent-behavior regression needs composition.

packages/core/src/datasets/ defines Dataset types and storage/domains/datasets/ persists them; runEvals(agent, dataset, scorers, …) in packages/core/src/evals/run/index.ts is the orchestrator. Results persist to storage/domains/scores/ for trend dashboards — a complete first-class regression suite.

_evaluation.py (1941 lines, decorated @experimental) ships EvalItem, LocalEvaluator, evaluate_agent, evaluate_workflow, evaluate_traces, evaluate_foundry_target. Solid coverage but flagged experimental, and the production path leans on Foundry evals managed-service.
Report marks 17.1 red: no first-party dataset/regression primitives. The community pattern is to use Braintrust/Phoenix/Langfuse/LangSmith partners consuming the SDK's traces.
Repo uses vitest for its own tests but ships no agent-eval primitive. The TS SDK has no Dataset/Evaluator/EvalRun types.

First-party pydantic-evals package: dataset.py with Dataset/Case (JSON/YAML serializable), evaluators/ (built-ins + custom + llm_judge), online.py for production traffic sampling, reports/ and otel/ for emission. Complete dataset+harness story.

crates/rig-core/src/evals.rs is feature-gated 'experimental' and ships an Eval trait with eval()/eval_batch() and an EvalOutcome enum. It is a primitive: there is no first-party golden-dataset file format or runner.
Report explicitly states 'Not provided. Standard pytest is used internally; no built-in eval harness.'
The TS SDK has unit + integration tests for its own code but no dataset format or runner for agent-behavior regression.
No SDK-shipped eval dataset format. @ai-sdk/test-server mocks providers for unit tests, but regression/eval harnesses are external (Braintrust, LangSmith, your own).
No first-party rubric/scorer/judge classifier ships in adk-go (report 17.2: 'Not provided — BYO').

AccuracyEval (eval/accuracy.py:24-58) uses an LLM (default the agent's model) to score outputs 1–10 against expected_output with reasoning. AgentAsJudge is a separate first-party judge class. Both are wired into the run/store flow.
Report 17.2: 'Not provided — BYO'. The evaluator/parallel.rs file exists but is for internal parallelism, not LLM-as-judge.
Report marks 17.2 red. No rubric scorer primitive ships in the SDK.
No first-party LLM-as-judge primitive in the TS SDK; users build it themselves over query().

CrewEvaluator instantiates an Agent(role='Task Execution Evaluator') that grades each task output 1–10 on completion/quality/overall performance using LLM-as-judge. The judge prompt is hardcoded; no rubric customization beyond task.expected_output. Patronus/AMP integrations exist for richer scoring.
Report 17.2: 'Not provided — BYO'. Eino ships no judge framework; you'd write your own function that calls an LLM with a rubric prompt.

Genkit Go has no shipped LLM-as-judge evaluator (JS side does). The recommended pattern is to define your own Evaluator whose Evaluate function calls genkit.Generate with a judge prompt and returns a Score — clean primitive, but BYO.
No LLM-as-judge in this repo. langchain has load_evaluator('labeled_score_string') but it's separately packaged; LangSmith ships hosted LLM-judges as paid.
Most of the shipped evaluators (RelevancyEvaluator, FaithfulnessEvaluator, CorrectnessEvaluator, GuidelineEvaluator, etc.) use an LLM as judge against a rubric. RAG-focused but production-ready.

createScorer({…}).generateScore(async ({ run }) => …) supports both code-based and LLM-based scorers (call another model with a rubric). Built-in scorers under packages/core/src/evals/. Uniquely, scorers can be wired into the loop via isTaskComplete so the agent re-iterates until passing.

Evaluator protocol (_evaluation.py:507) supports pre-built checks (keyword_check, tool_calls_present, tool_call_args_match) and custom LLM-judge functions. Solid, but in the experimental EVALS feature gate.
examples/agent_patterns/llm_as_a_judge.py shows the pattern using primitives (one agent grades another), but it is a usage example not a built-in scorer.
examples/agent-patterns/llm-as-a-judge.ts shows the pattern; users implement it from primitives. No SDK-shipped judge.
pydantic_evals.evaluators.llm_judge is a built-in evaluator (docs/evals/evaluators/llm-judge.md). First-class rubric scoring with reports + OTel.
Available via the evals module + Extractor: you implement Eval for a struct wrapping Extractor<M, YourRubric> to return Pass/Fail. It is a composable primitive, not a turnkey judge.
Report 17.2: 'Not provided — BYO'.
Report 17.2: 'Not provided'. No LLM-judge primitive in the TS SDK.
No first-party rubric primitive. Trivial to compose with generateObject({ model: judgeModel, schema, prompt }) but you write the rubric and harness.

No CI eval gate ships. The closest internal artifact is the replayplugin (internal/configurable/conformance/replayplugin/) for conformance replay, but it is internal-only and not exposed as a pre-merge gate.
No first-party 'pre-merge gate' CLI. You run evals via eval.run()/eval.arun() and assert on the returned score (e.g. result.score >= 8) inside pytest. Functional but DIY threshold.
Report 17.3: 'Not provided — BYO'. Standard cargo test runs unit tests, but no agent-behavior CI gates ship.
Report marks 17.3 red. No CI gate primitive ships.
Report 17.3: 'Not provided — BYO'. You build the gate yourself over query().

`crewai test` runs and prints a score table from CrewEvaluator, but the exit code is 0 unless an exception is raised — there is no --min-score threshold-fail. AMP markets 'Crew Testing' but no documented OSS CI integration with PR gates.
Report 17.3: 'Not provided'. The documented pattern is: in CI, run the agent against a fixture set, assert outputs match or judge-score above a threshold, block PR on failure — entirely BYO.

No first-party gate, but the recommended pattern (`genkit eval:run` JS CLI in CI, reading a JSON dataset and asserting on scores) is documented and the dataset/Evaluator primitives support it. You wire the CI yourself.
OSS-only: BYO pytest job that runs graph.invoke() against golden datasets and blocks merge on regression. No gate primitive ships; LangSmith (paid) provides gate-style workflows.
Not first-party as a gate, but BatchEvalRunner plus the eval primitives let you wire it into CI cleanly. No exit-code threshold helper ships.

runEvals runs cleanly inside Vitest it() blocks; the pattern is documented and eval results land in the configured storage backend for trend dashboards. There is no separate ScoredTest macro or gate CLI, so it's a strong test-harness integration rather than a turnkey gate.
Not packaged as a gate — you run evaluate_agent / evaluate_workflow in CI and fail on score. FoundryEvals provides a managed-service alternative for gating.
Report 17.3 red: 'BYO'.
Report 17.3: 'Not provided'.

Datasets can run under pytest; the framework's own suite uses inline-snapshot + pytest-recording + vcrpy for replay-based LLM testing (AGENTS.md:107-115), and that pattern is documented for integration into your CI. Strong test-harness story, not a packaged gate binary.
Not provided as a turnkey CI gate; you write a cargo test that calls eval_batch(...) and asserts. Pattern exists but the framework provides no gate helper.
